headline: Diesel export policy outranked every shipping signal yesterday
hook: Diesel export policy led the day: Argus Media reports Trump has moderated his calls for a US diesel export ban, and Reuters says Russia has extended its ban to the end of October.
board: Strait of Hormuz still carries the most lane pressure at 36, down from 51 the prior week, while Gulf of Aden fell from 12 to 1 and Red Sea & Suez rose from 6 to 9.
question: Would you lock in diesel cover now or wait for Russia's end-October decision?

items.headline: Russia keeps its diesel export ban through October
items.statLabel: New expiry of Russia's diesel export ban, per Reuters
items.what: Reuters reports that Russia has extended its diesel export ban until the end of October.
items.why: The extension keeps Russian diesel exports restricted for the rest of October. The material does not give volumes, scope or exemptions.
facts: Rated Elevated with a score of 11, in the Policy sector.
The second diesel export curb among the day's top three signals.
items.watch: Whether Russia extends the ban again when it expires at the end of October.

items.headline: Metals, petroleum and chemicals lift US rail volumes
items.statLabel: US weekly carloads and intermodal units, per AAR
items.what: Per AAR data reported by FreightWaves, US rail traffic for the week ending September 26 reached 537,397 units: 235,787 carloads (up 3% y/y) and 301,610 intermodal units (up 6.3%).
items.why: Gains came from metallic ores and metals (+9.5%), petroleum products (+9.4%) and chemicals (+7.2%). Coal carloads fell 2.1%, and domestic coal consumption was down 11.4% y/y.
facts: Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025.
First 38 weeks: 8,679,882 carloads (+2.7%) and 10,778,696 intermodal units (+4.1%).
North American weekly traffic on nine railroads: 733,610 units, up 3.5%.
items.watch: Coal in the next AAR weekly data: FreightWaves says the run-up to winter has been slow, with US coal production down 2.4% through Sept. 5.
